BOOKING REQUEST CHOOSER · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER

Which booking requests should you accept?

Two requests want the same week and one pays more. Or a 2-night request would leave a 1-night hole nobody can book. Paste your confirmed bookings and pending requests and see the exact set to accept for the most income, counting turnover cost, the dead gap nights each choice leaves, and counter-offers (a night earlier or later) worth sending the guests you would otherwise decline.

For hosts of vacation rentals, cabins, campsites, B&Bs, boats and event spaces. Nothing is uploaded: the text box is analysed in this browser and never leaves your device.

      Prefer a CLI?

      Same logic, zero dependencies, one command — reads a file or stdin:

      node cli.mjs plan calendar.csv --turnover 60 --night-value 50 --min-stay 3
cat calendar.csv | node cli.mjs plan - --json

      Get cli.mjs and engine.mjs — Node 18+, nothing to install, no network call. More: Which booking request should you accept? The gap-night math.

      What's recognised

      InputHandling

      The plan is exact for the numbers you type (dynamic programming over the gaps between confirmed bookings). Nights before the first and after the last stay in your paste are not counted. Platform fees, taxes, seasonal price changes and cancellations are not modelled; enter prices net of fees if you want a net result.

      Common questions

      Does it upload my bookings?

      No. The browser page works on the text you paste, in your own browser, and never sends it anywhere. The CLI reads a local file or stdin and makes no network call.

      Why would I decline a request that pays well?

      A stay that leaves one or two nights between it and the next booking creates a gap shorter than your minimum stay that nobody can book. Those nights earn nothing, so a lower-priced pair of stays that fit end to end can earn more than one high-priced stay that strands them.

      What is the empty-night value?

      Your own estimate of what a leftover night you can still sell is worth: your usual nightly price times how often leftover nights actually fill. Set it to zero to ignore gaps and only compare prices less turnover cost.

      Is the plan guaranteed to be best?

      It is the exact best answer for the numbers you typed, found by dynamic programming and checked against trying every combination in the tests. The numbers themselves are your estimates, so the result is a decision aid, not a forecast.

      Does it work for things other than short-term rentals?

      Yes for anything sold by the night with a minimum stay and a changeover cost: bed and breakfasts, cabins, campsites, boat and RV rentals, vacation homes and event spaces booked by the day.

It chooses between options using the numbers you supply; it is not a forecast of what will book.

      Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you type, or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as a system of record. If a tool needs to survive, get cli.mjs and run it yourself.

      Everything runs in your browser. The text you paste is never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (plan_run, example_loaded) are counted only in local storage and can be deleted with the button below. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control are honoured.

which-booking-request-to-accept.html.text:
Booking Request Chooser · guide

Which booking request should you accept? The gap-night math

Short answer: accept the set of requests that leaves the calendar worth the most, not the single request that pays the most. A stay is worth its price, less what it costs to turn the place over, plus whatever the nights it leaves behind can still earn. Nights trapped in a gap shorter than your minimum stay earn nothing.

A worked example

You have a 7-night hole between two confirmed bookings (5 to 12 July), a 3-night minimum, $60 turnover and leftover nights worth about $50.

  • Request A, 7 to 10 July, $480. It pays the most per night, but leaves 2 nights before and 2 after. Both gaps are under 3 nights, so 4 nights are dead. Worth $480 - $60 = $420.
  • Requests B (5 to 9 July, $440) and C (9 to 12 July, $345) fit end to end. Worth $785 - $120 = $665.

Accepting the first request that arrived, or the one with the highest price, costs $245 here. The Booking Request Chooser finds that answer on any calendar, exactly, and lists the reason for each decline.

How the plan is found

  1. Confirmed bookings are fixed. Any request overlapping one is out.
  2. Between each pair of confirmed bookings, the tool considers every chain of non-overlapping requests (a stay may end the day another begins) with dynamic programming, scoring price minus turnover plus the empty-night value of every leftover gap at least as long as your minimum stay.
  3. It compares that with accepting in arrival order and highest price first, and tries stays one or two nights longer or shorter at the guest's own nightly rate as counter-offers.

Pick the empty-night value honestly

That number is your estimate: your usual nightly price times how often a leftover night actually fills. Set it to zero and the tool only compares prices less turnover. The page also tells you whether the plan changes when leftover nights are worth nothing, half or double what you entered.

Questions

Should I accept the highest-paying booking request?

Not automatically. Compare what the calendar earns with and without it: its price, minus the cost of turning the place over, plus whatever the nights left on either side of it can still earn. If it leaves a gap shorter than your minimum stay, those nights are dead and the stay has to beat the alternative by more than their value.

How do I fill a one- or two-night gap between bookings?

Lower your minimum stay for just those dates, offer a discounted gap-night price, or send the guest a counter-offer that extends their stay a night earlier or later so it closes the gap.

Is it worth declining a request to keep a longer stay possible?

Only when the longer stays are realistic. Estimate what a leftover night is worth as your usual nightly price times how often leftover nights actually fill, and let the numbers decide.
